from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Geometry of a Vector", [
            "Visually, we represent a vector as an arrow.",
            "Every vector has a specific length, called magnitude.",
            "Every vector also points in a specific direction.",
            "You can slide a vector anywhere on the grid.",
            "It remains the same if magnitude and direction persist."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Visually, we represent a vector as an arrow.
        vector_color = "#00FFFF"
        vector = Arrow(self.grid["D3"], self.grid["B5"], buff=0, color=vector_color, stroke_width=8)
        vector_label = Text("Vector", font_size=24, color=vector_color)
        self.place_at_grid(vector_label, "C5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(vector_color)
        self.play(Create(vector), Write(vector_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Every vector has a specific length, called magnitude.
        mag_color = "#FFFF00"
        brace = BraceBetweenPoints(self.grid["D3"], self.grid["B5"], color=mag_color)
        mag_label = Text("Magnitude", font_size=20, color=mag_color).next_to(brace, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.lecture[1].set_color(mag_color)
        self.play(Create(brace), Write(mag_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Every vector also points in a specific direction.
        dir_color = "#FFA500"
        # Use a relative point for the reference line so it stays fixed to the vector's tail
        line_ref = DashedLine(self.grid["D3"], self.grid["D3"] + RIGHT * 1.5, color=WHITE, stroke_opacity=0.5)
        angle_arc = Arc(radius=0.5, start_angle=0, angle=PI/4, arc_center=self.grid["D3"], color=dir_color)
        dir_label = Text("Direction", font_size=20, color=dir_color)
        self.place_at_grid(dir_label, "E3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color(dir_color)
        self.play(Create(line_ref), Create(angle_arc), Write(dir_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # You can slide a vector anywhere on the grid.
        slide_color = "#00FF00"
        self.lecture[3].set_color(slide_color)
        
        # Group the vector and its properties (magnitude and direction indicators)
        vector_group = VGroup(vector, vector_label, brace, mag_label, line_ref, angle_arc, dir_label)
        
        # Slide to B1 (top-left area)
        shift_vector = self.grid["B1"] - self.grid["D3"]
        self.play(vector_group.animate.shift(shift_vector), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # It remains the same if magnitude and direction persist.
        persist_color = "#FF00FF"
        self.lecture[4].set_color(persist_color)
        
        # Slide to E4 (bottom-right area)
        shift_vector2 = self.grid["E4"] - self.grid["B1"]
        self.play(vector_group.animate.shift(shift_vector2), run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Algebra of Vectors: The 'Recipe'", 
                           ["We write vectors as a list of numbers.", 
                            "The numbers act as a recipe for movement.", 
                            "Component x moves right; component y moves up."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display a column matrix [4, 1] in #FFFFFF text on the side of the screen.
        matrix_41 = MathTex(r"\begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}", color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_41, 'B1', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(Write(matrix_41))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Trace a dashed #FFFFFF path moving 4 units right then 1 unit up.
        start_pt = self.grid['E2']
        mid_pt = self.grid['E6']
        end_pt = self.grid['D6']
        
        path_h = DashedLine(start_pt, mid_pt, color="#FFFFFF", dash_length=0.1)
        path_v = DashedLine(mid_pt, end_pt, color="#FFFFFF", dash_length=0.1)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(Create(path_h))
        self.play(Create(path_v))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Draw the resulting #FF4500 vector arrow over the traced path.
        vector_arrow = Arrow(start_pt, end_pt, color="#FF4500", buff=0)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF4500")) # Color matches the arrow
        self.play(GrowArrow(vector_arrow))

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Adding vectors is like following sequential instructions.",
            "Place the second vector's tail at the first's tip.",
            "The result is the arrow from start to end.",
            "Numerically, we simply add the corresponding components.",
            "This new vector represents the combined total movement."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Vector Addition: The Tip-to-Tail Method", lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_PLANE = "#1E90FF"
        COLOR_WIND = "#FF00FF"
        COLOR_RESULTANT = "#FFFF00"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = YELLOW

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Introductory line
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR))
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Draw Plane and Wind vectors
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_WIND)
        )
        
        # Positions
        plane_start = self.grid["D2"]
        plane_end = self.grid["D4"]
        wind_start = plane_end
        wind_end = self.grid["B4"]
        
        # Plane Vector
        plane_vec = Arrow(plane_start, plane_end, buff=0, color=COLOR_PLANE)
        plane_label = Text("Plane", font_size=20, color=COLOR_PLANE)
        self.place_at_grid(plane_label, "E3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Wind Vector
        wind_vec = Arrow(wind_start, wind_end, buff=0, color=COLOR_WIND)
        wind_label = Text("Wind", font_size=20, color=COLOR_WIND)
        self.place_at_grid(wind_label, "C5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(plane_vec), Write(plane_label))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(Create(wind_vec), Write(wind_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Draw Resultant vector
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_RESULTANT)
        )
        
        res_vec = Arrow(plane_start, wind_end, buff=0, color=COLOR_RESULTANT)
        res_label = Text("Resultant", font_size=20, color=COLOR_RESULTANT)
        self.place_at_grid(res_label, "C2", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(res_vec), Write(res_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Numerical addition
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_RESULTANT)
        )
        
        # Math: [2, 0] + [0, 2] = [2, 2]
        math_addition = MathTex(
            r"\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}", 
            "+", 
            r"\begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}", 
            "=", 
            r"\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}",
            font_size=32
        )
        # Apply colors to components
        math_addition[0].set_color(COLOR_PLANE)
        math_addition[2].set_color(COLOR_WIND)
        math_addition[4].set_color(COLOR_RESULTANT)
        
        self.place_in_area(math_addition, "F2", "F5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(math_addition))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Conclusion
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Visual emphasis on the resultant vector
        self.play(Flash(res_vec, color=COLOR_RESULTANT, line_length=0.3, flash_radius=0.4))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Section Title and Lecture Lines
        title_text = "Scalar Multiplication: Scaling the World"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Scalars are regular numbers that scale our vectors.",
            "Multiplying by a scalar stretches or shrinks the arrow.",
            "A scalar of two doubles the vector's length.",
            "Negative scalars flip the vector to the opposite direction.",
            "This scaling is the core of linear transformations."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Color Constants
        VECTOR_COLOR = "#ADFF2F"  # Greenish
        SCALAR_COLOR = "#FFD700"  # Gold
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Scalars are regular numbers that scale our vectors."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(SCALAR_COLOR))
        
        # Mathematical representation of the initial vector
        vec_v_math = MathTex(r"\vec{v} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}", color=VECTOR_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(vec_v_math, "A3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Create a coordinate system (NumberPlane) to visualize vectors
        # Fitting within area B3 to F6 (roughly 3x4 grid units)
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            y_range=[-7, 7, 1],
            x_length=3.5,
            y_length=4.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "stroke_width": 1.5, "color": GREY},
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.2}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, "B3", "F6")
        
        # The vector mobject
        v_arrow = plane.get_vector([1, 2], color=VECTOR_COLOR)
        v_label = MathTex(r"\vec{v}", color=VECTOR_COLOR)
        
        # Label updater to stay near the arrow tip
        def update_label(m):
            end_pos = v_arrow.get_end()
            # Dynamic placement to avoid overlapping the origin/axis
            direction = UR if end_pos[1] >= plane.get_origin()[1] else DL
            m.next_to(end_pos, direction, buff=0.1)
        
        v_label.add_updater(update_label)

        self.play(Write(vec_v_math))
        self.play(Create(plane))
        self.play(GrowArrow(v_arrow), FadeIn(v_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Multiplying by a scalar stretches or shrinks the arrow."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(SCALAR_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Scalar tracker for smooth animation
        k_tracker = ValueTracker(1.0)
        
        # Scalar variable display (using DecimalNumber for performance)
        scalar_label = MathTex("k =", color=SCALAR_COLOR)
        scalar_val = DecimalNumber(1.0, color=SCALAR_COLOR, num_decimal_places=1)
        scalar_val.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_value(k_tracker.get_value()))
        scalar_group = VGroup(scalar_label, scalar_val).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(scalar_group, "A5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Result expression k*v placeholder
        res_math = MathTex(r"k \cdot \vec{v}", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(res_math, "A4", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # Updater to scale the vector arrow geometry based on k
        def update_arrow(m):
            k = k_tracker.get_value()
            new_arrow = plane.get_vector([k * 1, k * 2], color=VECTOR_COLOR)
            m.become(new_arrow)
            
        v_arrow.add_updater(update_arrow)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(scalar_group), Write(res_math))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "A scalar of two doubles the vector's length."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(SCALAR_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Animate scalar growing to 2
        self.play(k_tracker.animate.set_value(2.0), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "Negative scalars flip the vector to the opposite direction."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(SCALAR_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Animate scalar flipping to -1
        self.play(k_tracker.animate.set_value(-1.0), run_time=2.0)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "This scaling is the core of linear transformations."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(VECTOR_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Animate scalar to 3.0 as specified in storyboard [3, 6]
        self.play(k_tracker.animate.set_value(3.0), run_time=2.0)
        
        # Final result mathematical formula
        final_res_math = MathTex(r"3 \cdot \vec{v} = \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 6 \end{bmatrix}", color=VECTOR_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(final_res_math, "A4", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(res_math, final_res_math))
        self.wait(2)

        # Cleanup updaters to avoid runtime overhead after animation
        v_arrow.remove_updater(update_arrow)
        v_label.remove_updater(update_label)
        scalar_val.clear_updaters()
from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Real-World Application", [
            "Vectors are both geometric arrows and numerical lists.",
            "They power physics engines, graphics, and data science.",
            "Mastering vectors unlocks the heart of linear algebra."
        ])
        
        # Colors
        color1 = "#FFFFFF"
        color2 = "#00FF00"
        color3 = "#00FF00" 

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a #FFFFFF arrow alongside its #FFFFFF [x, y] matrix.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(color1))
        
        vec_arrow = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 1.2, buff=0, color=color1)
        vec_matrix = MathTex(r"\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \end{bmatrix}", color=color1)
        
        self.place_at_grid(vec_arrow, "C2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(vec_matrix, "C4", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(
            GrowArrow(vec_arrow),
            Write(vec_matrix)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Display a #00FF00 grid of arrows representing a force field, 
        # incorporating the physics icon [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/physics.svg].
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(color2))
        
        # Group to hold the grid (3x3 for efficiency)
        force_field = VGroup()
        for i in range(3):
            for j in range(3):
                pos_x = i - 1.0
                pos_y = j - 1.0
                # Rotational field direction
                direction = np.array([-pos_y, pos_x, 0])
                norm = np.linalg.norm(direction)
                if norm > 0:
                    direction = direction / norm * 0.5
                else:
                    direction = RIGHT * 0.5
                
                arrow = Arrow(ORIGIN, direction, buff=0, color=color2, stroke_width=3)
                arrow.move_to(np.array([pos_x, pos_y, 0]))
                force_field.add(arrow)
        
        self.place_in_area(force_field, "B2", "E4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Load physics icon from specified path
        physics_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/physics.svg")
        physics_icon.set_color(color2)
        self.place_at_grid(physics_icon, "D5", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(
            FadeOut(vec_arrow),
            FadeOut(vec_matrix),
            LaggedStart(*[GrowArrow(a) for a in force_field], lag_ratio=0.05),
            FadeIn(physics_icon)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Scale the #00FF00 grid to show a linear transformation.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(color3))
        
        # Group content for transformation
        scene_content = VGroup(force_field, physics_icon)
        
        # Apply transformation (scaling and shear using apply_matrix to illustrate linear algebra concepts)
        # Shear along X-axis by 0.3: x' = x + 0.3y, y' = y
        shear_matrix = [[1, 0.3, 0], 
                        [0, 1, 0], 
                        [0, 0, 1]]
        
        self.play(
            scene_content.animate.scale(1.2).apply_matrix(shear_matrix),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: The Visual Heart of Linear Algebra: Understanding Vectors
outline.target_audience: First-year university students or advanced high school students interested in STEM

sections.title: Prerequisite: From Points to Directions
sections.content: Briefly revisit the Cartesian coordinate system. Distinguish between a 'point' (a static location) and a 'vector' (an instruction for movement). Explain that while a point is a destination, a vector is the journey.
sections.example: Imagine a cat sitting at coordinate (0,0). To get to a bowl of milk at (3,2), the cat must move 3 units right and 2 units up. That specific instruction—the movement itself—is our vector.

sections.title: The Geometry of a Vector
sections.content: Introduce the visual representation of a vector as an arrow in space. Emphasize two critical properties: Magnitude (length of the arrow) and Direction (where it points). Explain that vectors can slide around the graph as long as length and angle remain the same.
sections.example: Visualize a gust of wind represented by an arrow. Whether the wind blows at the park or the beach, if it's 20mph heading North-East, it's the same vector.

sections.title: The Algebra of Vectors: The 'Recipe'
sections.content: Translate the visual arrow into a numerical list (a column matrix). Explain the [x, y] notation as a 'recipe' for movement. Show how the vector [3, -2] translates to '3 steps forward, 2 steps down' on the grid.
sections.example: A game character 'Hero_A' has a movement vector of [4, 1]. In an animation, we show a ghost overlay of the hero moving 4 units along the x-axis and 1 unit up the y-axis to reach their new position.

sections.title: Vector Addition: The Tip-to-Tail Method
sections.content: Demonstrate how to combine two vectors. Visually, place the 'tail' of the second vector at the 'tip' of the first. Numerically, show that we simply add the corresponding x and y components.
sections.example: A plane is flying with a velocity vector [10, 0] (moving straight East). A crosswind hits it with a vector [0, 2] (moving North). The resulting path of the plane is the diagonal arrow formed by [10+0, 0+2] = [10, 2].

sections.title: Scalar Multiplication: Scaling the World
sections.content: Introduce 'Scalars' (regular numbers). Show how multiplying a vector by a scalar stretches, shrinks, or flips the direction (if the scalar is negative). This is the 'linear' part of linear algebra.
sections.example: If a rocket's thrust vector is [1, 2], and we activate 'Turbo Mode' (a scalar of 3), the new vector becomes [3, 6]. Visually, the arrow grows three times longer but maintains the same slope.

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Application
sections.content: Summarize how vectors serve as the building blocks for computer graphics, physics engines, and data science. Reiterate that a vector is both a geometric arrow and a list of numbers.
sections.example: Show a quick montage: a 3D character model made of thousands of vectors, a weather map of wind velocities, and a search engine ranking results based on 'vector similarity'.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: From Points to Directions
lecture_lines: A point represents a static location in space.
A vector is different; it represents movement.
Think of it as a journey, not a destination.
animations: Show a #FFFFFF point at (0,0) labeled 'Location'.
Draw a #FFD700 vector arrow starting from the #FFFFFF point.

storyboard.title: The Geometry of a Vector
lecture_lines: Visually, we represent a vector as an arrow.
Every vector has a specific length, called magnitude.
Every vector also points in a specific direction.
You can slide a vector anywhere on the grid.
It remains the same if magnitude and direction persist.
animations: Draw a #00FFFF arrow labeled 'Vector' in the center.
Highlight the #00FFFF arrow's length and label it 'Magnitude'.
Flash the #00FFFF arrow's tip and label its angle 'Direction'.

storyboard.title: The Algebra of Vectors: The 'Recipe'
lecture_lines: We write vectors as a list of numbers.
The numbers act as a recipe for movement.
Component x moves right; component y moves up.
animations: Display a #FFFFFF column matrix [4, 1] on the side, accompanied by [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/recipe.svg].
Trace a dashed #FFFFFF path 4 units right from origin.
Draw the resulting #FF4500 vector arrow over the path.

storyboard.title: Vector Addition: The Tip-to-Tail Method
lecture_lines: Adding vectors is like following sequential instructions.
Place the second vector's tail at the first's tip.
The result is the arrow from start to end.
Numerically, we simply add the corresponding components.
This new vector represents the combined total movement.
animations: Draw a #1E90FF vector labeled 'A' starting from origin.
Place a #FF00FF vector 'B' at 'A's tip.
Draw a #FFFF00 vector from origin to 'B's tip.
Display addition: [x1+x2, y1+y2] in #FFFFFF near the vectors.
Flash the #FFFF00 resultant vector to show total movement.

storyboard.title: Scalar Multiplication: Scaling the World
lecture_lines: Scalars are regular numbers that scale our vectors.
Multiplying by a scalar stretches or shrinks the arrow.
A scalar of two doubles the vector's length.
Negative scalars flip the vector to the opposite direction.
This scaling is the core of linear transformations.
animations: Show a #ADFF2F vector 'v' and scalar 'k' positioned over the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/world.svg] icon.
Animate the #ADFF2F vector changing length based on 'k'.
Scale the #ADFF2F vector to exactly twice its length.
Flip the #ADFF2F vector to point in the opposite direction.
Pulse the scaled #ADFF2F vector to emphasize the transformation.
